The rechecking fee is not refunded if rechecking produces no increase in marks, because the rechecking fee is refunded only if there is an increase in marks [S1].

diagnostics.history_context:
Student: I registered for FYP-I but have not passed it yet. Can I register for FYP-II because registration is already on my record?
Assistant (context only): Registration on your record for FYP-I does not automatically allow you to register for FYP-II, because registration in FYP-II is allowed only after the successful completion of FYP-I .

Student: Can I replace a failed core course with an elective that I passed later?
Assistant (context only): A core course cannot be replaced by any other course . According to the regulations, a core course cannot be replaced by any other course , and before submitting a course replacement request to the Dean for approval, several conditions must be fulfilled, including that the grade in the course to be replaced is 'F' and that the replacing course was passed at least one semester after the course to be replaced was taken .

Student: I want to withdraw before the deadline, but I receive financial support. Is meeting the deadline sufficient?
Assistant (context only): Meeting the deadline is not sufficient to withdraw from a course if you receive financial support, because students on any form of financial support are not allowed to withdraw from any course .

Student: If I withdraw from a course, does that erase the course from my transcript?
Assistant (context only): Withdrawing from a course does not erase it from your transcript, because a grade of "W" will be awarded for withdrawn courses and will appear on the transcript, though it will not affect the CGPA .

Student: I repeated a course and earned the same grade as before. Do both attempts count separately in CGPA?
Assistant (context only): When you repeat a course, both attempts do not count separately in your CGPA because only the most recent grade points are used for repeated courses in CGPA calculation, even if they are less than the earlier attempts .

Student: I missed paper viewing. Have I permanently lost the right to request rechecking?
Assistant (context only): You have not permanently lost the right to request rechecking if you missed paper viewing, because a student who has not viewed their final exam paper in the scheduled paper viewing session may still request rechecking of the final examination by paying the prescribed fee . To proceed, your application must reach the Examination Office within seven days of the announcement of the result and must be submitted on the prescribed form together with the rechecking fee  .

FAQs
Is There Any Information For The Parent Of A Student?
CFD campus welcomes parents at the campus on any day for student's academic information
or record discussion. It is suggested that parents must visit the student's profile on LMS.
Do Employers Recruit Students On Campus?
The career services Office regularly shares available employment opportunities offered by
leading organizations. It actively arranges recruitment drives and professional development
seminars. Campus annually organizes the Job Fair to facilitate the recruitment process
of our graduating batch.

You can communicate with the OSAF (Old Student Association of FAST NUCES).

several societies, covering a wide variety of interests, are available for students to join or
attend. Social, sports, and literature based clubs also exist. The campus also provides you
clubs like ACM and IEEE that bridge between academic and industry.
Who Should I Contact In Case Of Any Complaint/ Harassment Or Ragging?
The issue can be taken up with hostel warden or batch advisors. In case of serious issues you
can email to HoD/Director Campus.

Campus organizes multiple events annually such as orientation ceremony, welcome parties
for newcomers, recreational tours, technical competitions, sports events, annual leagues,
farewells and much more. The region's biggest Olympiad DAIRA is organized every year.
What Are Allied Facilities At Campus?
Computing labs, engineering labs, common rooms, sports grounds, fitness center, medical
center, mosque, library, discussion rooms, transportation, hostel, and research labs.

diagnostics.history_context:
Student: My parent campus offers the summer course, but another campus is more convenient. Does the documented permission cover that reason?
Assistant (context only): The documented permission does not cover taking a summer course at another campus simply because it is more convenient when the parent campus offers it . According to the rules for the summer semester, a student can study a summer semester at another campus only under the condition that the parent campus is not offering that course, and the student must also obtain prior permission in writing from the Director of the parent campus .

Student: Does a high CGPA give me an unconditional right to transfer to another FAST campus?
Assistant (context only): A high CGPA does not give an undergraduate student an unconditional right to transfer to another FAST campus . Transfer requests are considered only on specific grounds: the death of a parent, the posting of a parent to the city where the transfer is desired, or the marriage of a female student . Furthermore, a transfer request will be considered by the Competent Authority provided that the Directors of both campuses have no objection, there is a place available at the destination campus, and none of the following disqualifying cases apply: the student is under disciplinary punishment, disciplinary action is pending, dues are outstanding, or the request is made during the course of a semester .

Student: My merit-scholarship SGPA requirement is satisfied, but I took more credits than the prescribed load. Is the GPA condition enough?
Assistant (context only): The GPA condition is not enough to maintain the merit scholarship because taking more credits than the prescribed load makes a student ineligible  . According to the rules, a student registering for less or more credit hours than the total specified number of credit hours is not eligible for the Merit Scholarship  . Additionally, continuation of the merit scholarship is subject to maintaining a semester GPA of 3.0 or higher, and the student must not have failed, repeated, or withdrawn from a course in that semester   .

**Related conditions and exceptions from the retrieved sources:**

> This scholarship is for four years of un-interrupted studies with standard courses (core and elective), labs and final year projects of the degree offered by the department in a semester to a batch with a specified number of total credit hours and is equal to the full tuition fee. 

Student: I receive tuition assistance. Does that mean my hostel gym membership is also funded?
Assistant (context only): Receiving tuition assistance does not mean your hostel gym membership is funded, because students may avail the hostel gym facility by paying a maintenance fee of Rs. 5,000 per semester or Rs. 2,000 per month, along with a one-time registration fee of Rs. 1,000 .

Student: My study loan was approved last semester. Can I assume it renews without another review?
Assistant (context only): A study loan does not automatically renew without another review, because financial assistance in the form of a loan is subject to renewal every semester in the light of the student's academic performance and financial need . Additionally, this financial assistance is discontinued if the student's CGPA falls below 2.00 for an undergraduate degree .

Student: I graduate but remain unemployed for six months. Does repayment wait until I find a job?
Assistant (context only): Repayment of the study loan does not wait until you find a job if you remain unemployed for six months, because the repayment of the loan starts three months after graduation or soon after getting employment, whichever is earlier   . Under these rules, once three months have passed following your graduation, your repayment schedule begins regardless of your employment status   . Additionally, the total amount must be repaid within a period of four years after graduation   .
